items.title: Executive dysfunction
items.summary: Difficulty initiating, sequencing, remembering, switching, estimating time, or sustaining attention can occur even when a task matters deeply.
signals: knows what to do but cannot start
support_actions: externalize steps
shrink the first action
use cues, timers, body doubling, and visible checklists
items.boundary: Support strategies do not establish or rule out an ADHD diagnosis.

items.title: Sensory overload
items.summary: Sound, light, touch, temperature, smell, movement, internal sensations, and social demands can accumulate until processing and communication capacity fall.
support_actions: reduce stimulation
lower demands
offer alternate communication
protect recovery time
items.boundary: Do not treat overload behavior as deliberate misconduct by default.

items.title: Autistic burnout
items.summary: Long-term overload, masking, inaccessible environments, and insufficient recovery can produce marked loss of capacity.
support_actions: reduce nonessential demands
increase accommodations
protect recovery
seek professional help for major functional decline or medical concerns

items.title: Cognitive model
items.summary: Thoughts, emotions, body sensations, behaviors, and context influence one another. CBT tools can examine one link without assuming every distressing thought is inaccurate.
support_actions: separate observations from interpretations
test predictions safely
use balanced alternatives
pair cognitive work with behavior change

items.title: Dialectics
items.summary: Two apparently opposing things can both contain truth, such as accepting the present while working to change it.
support_actions: validate what is true now
identify what needs change
avoid all-or-nothing framing

items.title: Functional impact
items.summary: Symptom severity is better understood when paired with what changed in sleep, relationships, self-care, work/school, decision-making, safety, and daily functioning.
support_actions: track baseline and change
bring concrete examples to clinicians

items.title: Psychosis-aware support
items.summary: When someone reports hallucinations, paranoia, or unusual beliefs, emotional validation can be paired with reality-based language.
support_actions: acknowledge distress
do not confirm implausible claims as fact
focus on observable safety
seek professional help when new, worsening, or dangerous

items.title: Mania or severe activation
items.summary: Markedly reduced need for sleep, unusually high or irritable energy, racing thoughts, grandiosity, pressured speech, or risky behavior can warrant prompt professional assessment, especially when new or escalating.
support_actions: reduce stimulation
involve trusted support
avoid encouraging risky plans
seek urgent professional help if safety or judgment is impaired

items.title: Dissociation
items.summary: Detachment, unreality, fogginess, time loss, or feeling disconnected can be frightening and can reduce functioning.
support_actions: orient to present facts
use tolerable sensory anchors
reduce demands
seek professional support for persistent, severe, or dangerous episodes

items.title: Grief variability
items.summary: Grief can include sadness, anger, numbness, relief, guilt, longing, physical fatigue, and changing intensity over time.
support_actions: support basic care
make room for different grief responses
seek additional help when safety or functioning is severely affected

items.title: Symptom triage boundary
items.summary: A chatbot can help organize symptoms but should not replace urgent medical evaluation or a clinician-specific plan.
support_actions: document onset and associated symptoms
follow existing medical plan
escalate clear emergencies immediately
items.boundary: No medication dosing, diagnosis, or personalized emergency thresholds are generated by this brain.

items.title: Tiny Start support note
items.summary: Task initiation is blocked by overwhelm, perfectionism, low energy, or unclear first steps.
support_actions: Name the task in one sentence.
Shrink it until the first action takes about two minutes or less.
Place only the needed item or screen in front of the person.

items.title: Working Memory Externalization support note
items.summary: The person keeps losing steps, ideas, or intentions.
support_actions: Capture the thought immediately outside the brain.
Keep one visible list for the current task.
Cross off or hide completed steps.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not rely on 'just remember'.

items.title: Transition Bridge support note
items.summary: Stopping one activity and beginning another is hard.
support_actions: Name the current activity and the next activity.
Give a predictable warning.
Choose one bridge action such as save, bathroom, drink, stretch, or pack materials.

items.title: Body Double support note
items.summary: Presence helps task initiation or persistence.
support_actions: Agree on the task and duration.
The support person stays present without taking over.
Use brief check-ins rather than constant reminders.

items.title: Time Map support note
items.summary: Time blindness makes planning unreliable.
support_actions: Estimate the task in chunks.
Add setup, transition, and recovery time.
Anchor to a real event or alarm.

items.title: Sensory Map support note
items.summary: Overload, shutdown, irritability, pain, or fatigue may be affected by sensory input.
support_actions: Check sound, light, touch, temperature, smell, movement, hunger, thirst, pain, and social load.
Identify one input to reduce and one regulating input to add.
Lower communication demand while regulating.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not force eye contact or verbal explanation during overload.

items.title: Shutdown Support support note
items.summary: Speech, movement, decision-making, or processing has dropped sharply under stress.
support_actions: Reduce demands and questions.
Offer yes/no, pointing, typing, AAC, or silence.
Reduce sensory load and preserve physical safety.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not interpret reduced speech as defiance.

items.title: Meltdown Recovery support note
items.summary: The nervous system is overloaded and behavioral control is reduced.
support_actions: Prioritize safety and lower stimulation.
Reduce audience and demands.
Allow safe regulating movement or stillness.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not use punishment, argument, or forced processing during peak overload.

items.title: Burnout Load Reduction support note
items.summary: Sustained overload, masking, demands, or insufficient recovery have reduced capacity.
support_actions: List essential and deferrable demands.
Protect recovery time and sensory safety.
Use communication shortcuts and accessibility supports.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not frame reduced capacity as laziness.

items.title: Predictable Transition support note
items.summary: Change or uncertainty is increasing distress.
support_actions: Describe what will happen, in what order, and what is uncertain.
Name a fallback plan.
Allow a regulating object, routine, or communication method.

items.title: Thought Record support note
items.summary: A strong emotion is linked to a specific interpretation or prediction.
support_actions: Describe the situation briefly.
Name the automatic thought.
Rate emotion intensity.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not use cognitive restructuring to argue someone out of a real safety concern or discrimination experience.

items.title: Behavioral Activation support note
items.summary: Low mood or avoidance has reduced meaningful activity.
support_actions: Choose one very small activity tied to care, mastery, connection, or pleasure.
Set a low-effort version.
Schedule a specific start cue.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not prescribe exertion that conflicts with medical or disability limits.

items.title: Structured Problem Solving support note
items.summary: A solvable problem is looping without a concrete plan.
support_actions: Define the problem narrowly.
Brainstorm options without judging them.
Compare effort, safety, accessibility, and likely benefit.

items.title: Worry Window support note
items.summary: Repetitive worry is consuming the day.
support_actions: Capture the worry in a note.
Choose a short scheduled time to review worries.
During the day, redirect to the present task when possible.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not postpone urgent safety or medical concerns.

items.title: Graded Practice support note
items.summary: Avoidance is maintaining fear and the target is safe, consensual, and appropriate for gradual practice.
support_actions: Define the feared but safe activity.
Create small steps from easier to harder.
Choose a manageable step and coping support.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not use for trauma processing, medical risk, abuse situations, psychosis content, self-harm urges, or unsafe environments without qualified clinical guidance.

items.title: STOP support note
items.summary: A strong urge may lead to an impulsive action.
support_actions: Stop.
Take a step back physically or mentally.
Observe body sensations, emotions, thoughts, urges, and facts.

items.title: TIPP support note
items.summary: High physiological arousal needs short-term downshifting.
support_actions: Use a safe temperature change that does not conflict with medical needs.
Use brief movement only within physical capacity.
Slow the exhale and pace breathing comfortably.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not use intense exercise or extreme temperature when medically unsafe; use gentler grounding instead.

items.title: ACCEPTS support note
items.summary: Short-term distraction is needed to survive a distress spike without making things worse.
support_actions: Choose a safe activity, contribution, comparison, emotion shift, temporary pushing-away, different thoughts, or sensory focus.
Use it as a temporary bridge.
Return to the problem later if action is needed.

items.title: Check the Facts support note
items.summary: Emotion intensity may be amplified by assumptions or incomplete information.
support_actions: Name the prompting event.
Separate observations from interpretations.
Check assumptions against available evidence.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not dismiss lived experience or real danger as a thinking error.

items.title: Opposite Action support note
items.summary: An emotion or urge does not fit the facts or acting on it would be ineffective.
support_actions: Name the emotion and urge.
Check the facts and safety.
Identify the effective opposite behavior.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not use opposite action to override legitimate boundaries, pain limits, medical symptoms, or danger signals.

items.title: DEAR MAN support note
items.summary: A clear request, refusal, or boundary is needed.
support_actions: Describe the facts briefly.
Express feelings or impact.
Assert the request or boundary clearly.

items.title: GIVE support note
items.summary: The relationship matters during a conversation.
support_actions: Be gentle.
Show interest.
Validate what makes sense in the other person's experience.

items.title: FAST support note
items.summary: Self-respect needs protection in an interpersonal situation.
support_actions: Be fair to self and others.
Avoid unnecessary apologies for existing or having needs.
Stick to values.

items.title: Behavior Chain Analysis support note
items.summary: A behavior needs a no-blame map of what led to it and what could change next time.
support_actions: Name the target behavior neutrally.
Identify vulnerabilities before the event.
Map prompting event, thoughts, body sensations, emotions, actions, and consequences.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not turn chain analysis into interrogation, punishment, or proof of moral failure.

items.title: Structured Psychiatric Check-In support note
items.summary: The person wants to summarize symptoms and functioning for themselves or a clinician.
support_actions: Review mood, anxiety, irritability, energy, sleep, appetite, concentration, trauma symptoms, dissociation, unusual perceptions/thoughts, substance use, and safety.
Record onset, frequency, intensity, duration, triggers, and functional impact.
Note medication taken as prescribed, missed doses, and side effects without changing treatment.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not convert a checklist score into a diagnosis.

items.title: Clinician Visit Preparation support note
items.summary: A visit is coming up and important information needs organization.
support_actions: List the top three concerns.
Add timeline, examples, and functional impact.
List current medications and side effects exactly as taken/reported.

items.title: Medication Journal support note
items.summary: The person wants to track medication experience without changing treatment.
support_actions: Record medication name exactly as prescribed, time taken, missed dose if any, perceived benefit, side effects, sleep, appetite, and relevant symptoms.
Mark urgent reactions for professional or emergency review.
Bring trends to the prescriber or pharmacist.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not advise dose changes, taper schedules, substitutions, or combining substances.

items.title: Reality-Grounded Support support note
items.summary: A person reports paranoia, hallucinations, or unusual beliefs.
support_actions: Acknowledge fear or distress.
Avoid confirming the unusual belief as fact.
Focus on what is directly observable and immediate safety.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not investigate, elaborate, or role-play the delusional framework as true.

items.title: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding support note
items.summary: The person feels flooded, panicky, detached, or stuck in looping thoughts and sensory grounding is tolerable.
support_actions: Notice five things you can see.
Notice four things you can feel safely.
Notice three things you can hear.

items.title: Dissociation Anchor support note
items.summary: The person feels unreal, detached, foggy, or disconnected.
support_actions: State the current date and location if known.
Name one reliable fact about the present moment.
Press feet, hands, or another supported body area into a stable surface if comfortable.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not force intense sensory stimulation.

items.title: Grief Support support note
items.summary: Loss is producing waves of sadness, numbness, anger, longing, or disorientation.
support_actions: Name what hurts most right now.
Choose care for the next hour rather than solving grief.
Use memory, ritual, connection, rest, food, hydration, or practical support as wanted.

items.title: Sleep Wind-Down support note
items.summary: The person wants a low-pressure sleep routine.
support_actions: Choose a repeatable wind-down cue.
Reduce stimulating tasks when possible.
Prepare accessibility, medications as prescribed, hydration, bathroom, temperature, and sensory needs before settling.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not present sleep hygiene as a cure for psychiatric or medical sleep disorders.

items.title: Symptom Journal support note
items.summary: Symptoms need organized tracking for self-management or a clinician.
support_actions: Record symptom, start time, intensity, duration, location, triggers, associated symptoms, function impact, and what helped or worsened it.
Add relevant device readings only if already part of the person's care plan.
Mark new severe or rapidly worsening symptoms for prompt professional review.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not use the journal to delay emergency care.

items.title: Accessibility-Aware Care Plan support note
items.summary: A care task conflicts with mobility, pain, fatigue, sensory, communication, or caregiver limits.
support_actions: Define the goal rather than one required method.
Identify access barriers.
Create seated, bed-based, AAC, low-energy, or assisted alternatives where appropriate.

items.title: Follow Existing Medical Plan support note
items.summary: A health condition already has clinician instructions.
support_actions: Use the written plan as the source of truth for thresholds, medication, devices, and escalation.
Record what happened and what action the plan directs.
Contact the relevant clinician/pharmacist when instructions are unclear or symptoms are changing.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not invent personalized thresholds, correction doses, missed-dose instructions, or device settings.

items.title: Medical Emergency Escalation support note
items.summary: Clear emergency symptoms may be present.
support_actions: Stop chatbot problem solving.
Contact local emergency services now.
Get a nearby person if possible.
items.boundary: Avoid: Do not reassure away severe symptoms or delay emergency help for a worksheet.
